input: Use only the frozen synthetic snapshot in incident.json; do not run network tools or claim live validation. Write diagnosis.json as one JSON object with exactly these top-level keys: status, scope, finding, supporting_observations, unknowns, next_check, actions_taken, recommended_actions. Field meanings: status says whether the supplied observations establish a local blocker; choose supported_local_blocker or insufficient_evidence. Copy scope from incident.json. finding has exactly class and boundary; class must be one of service_listener, network_filter, route_path, name_resolution, application_health, insufficient_evidence, and boundary names the affected component or boundary. supporting_observations is a list of observation IDs that substantiate the finding. unknowns lists every field identified as not supplied. next_check has exactly operation and read_only, with one safe, non-mutating follow-up. No changes are authorized: actions_taken and recommended_actions must be empty arrays. Do not infer that unobserved layers are healthy, and do not recommend a restart, configuration change, firewall change, or other mutation. Only diagnosis.json may change. In your final answer, return exactly one JSON object and no surrounding prose with exactly these keys: status (copy diagnosis.json), scope (copy incident.json), runtime_validation (not_performed), and recommended_action (none). Do not add keys or free-form claims. Boundary must be an affirmative scope label; do not use negation or a disclaimer. next_check.operation must be exactly one of: review_captured_observations, compare_time_stamped_states, trace_request_path, inspect_related_configuration. Set read_only to true and do not add command text or extra instructions to operation. Evidence relationships: cite the observation that links the initiating peer to the target address or source tuple, the time-stamped listener state or matching filter observation, and the failed request plus any paired counter change. If supplied configuration and a later runtime observation differ, cite both and distinguish configured intent from what was observed at runtime. In finding.boundary, identify the component and its specific interface, namespace, chain, or other scope; a service name and port alone are too broad.
target: Produce a bounded, evidence-supported diagnosis from the frozen local snapshot.
